data.title: The stolen helmet from Bojná has been reconstructed
data.excerpt: A 9th-century helmet found at Bojná by an illegal metal detectorist around the year 2000 was never reported and was most probably sold to Germany; a single auction photograph is almost the only evidence that it existed. A Czech enthusiast gathered all the available information about it and had a replica made, which is now on display in the Museum of Great Moravia at Bojná.
data.metaTitle: The stolen helmet from Bojná reconstructed
data.metaDescription: A 9th-century helmet from Bojná was found by an illegal metal detectorist around 2000 and sold abroad; a replica is now on show in the museum at Bojná.

children.text: Probably sometime around the year 2000 an illegal metal detectorist found a 9th-century helmet at Bojná. He did not report the find to archaeologists and appropriated it. He then most probably sold it to Germany, and since then the helmet has literally “vanished without a trace”. Because he sold it through an auction site, one photograph appeared on the internet at the time of the sale, and that, together with the claims of some witnesses, is the only evidence of its existence.

Tomáš Vlasatý, an enthusiast from the Czech Republic, took the trouble to obtain all the available information about the helmet and had a replica of it made on that basis. A large number of volunteers contributed financially to its production. He then donated it to the Museum of Great Moravia in Bojná, where you can see it in person. Perhaps one day it will be possible to track down the original as well, which is now without doubt in some private collection in the “West”. This is how metal detectorists are costing us the treasures of our history.
